analyst_view.overall: Early view: Panathinaikos (2nd, nine points) have won all three league-phase games and lead the Greek league with 20 goals for and four against in nine games. Nordsjælland (25th, two points) are fifth in Denmark and drew at Hearts and at home to CSKA before a 2-0 defeat at Monaco. The site's numbers make Nordsjælland slight favourites at home; on form I would rate Panathinaikos at least level.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I lean a little lower: Panathinaikos concede very little (four goals in nine league games, three in three European games) and Nordsjælland failed to score at Monaco. Panathinaikos's 5-1 at Kairat was the exception rather than their usual pattern.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, split evenly. I read nothing about either side's style that moves this, so I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards, a little more for Panathinaikos. No referee is known yet and neither side's European games have been notably ill-tempered, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.0 shots. Nordsjælland at home will want the ball, while Panathinaikos have been efficient rather than shot-heavy; the number looks about right.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target. Without team news I see nothing to move it; Panathinaikos's tight defence argues slightly down, Nordsjælland's need to chase the game slightly up.
